lens: Lens 3 — free probability and derandomization (Wang–Lau–Zhou, arXiv 2601.08111) against the third-cumulant memory. Scripts and logs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/lens3/ (lib3.py: kprop3 with a per-layer readout switch, verified bit-exact against whest/kprop3.py; e1_free_closure.py -> e1.log, net 0 n=1024; e2_effect_parity.py -> e2_s1.log, e2_s2.log, n=256 L=8 synthetic He nets, M=64/48 resamples; e3_wick_mean.py -> e3_s1.log; e4_net0_wick.py -> e4.log, net 0 layer 4, M=8). All chains float64, OMP_NUM_THREADS=2.

claims.claim: (a1) The LINEAR step of the Gaussian closure, S_{l+1} = W C_l W^T with W iid N(0,2/n), is exactly an operator-valued (matrix) Dyson fixed point that collapses to the scalar Marchenko–Pastur–Silverstein equation g(z) = 1/(z - (2/n) sum_i c_i/(z - 2 g c_i)), c_i = eig(C_l), where z m_S(z^2) = g(z) is the Hermitised resolvent of S_{l+1}; equivalently law(S_{l+1}) = (2 MP_1) boxtimes law(C_l).
claims.argument: Hermitise H = [[0, W C^{1/2}],[C^{1/2} W^T, 0]] = sum_ab W_ab A_ab with symmetric coefficient matrices A_ab = [[0, E_ab C^{1/2}],[C^{1/2} E_ba, 0]]. The MDE G = (z - sum_ab (2/n) A_ab G A_ab)^{-1} has self-energy diag((2/n) tr(C G_2) I, (2/n) tr(G_1) C) because sum_ab E_ab M E_ba = tr(M) I (the covariance map of an iid matrix is a trace, as the free-derandomization reader noted: eta(M) = (2/n) tr(M) I); with G_1 = g I this is the scalar equation above. CHECKED on net 0 (e1.log part 1): relative residual of the fixed point against the empirical z m_S(z^2) is 1.3e-3/4.5e-4/1.3e-4 at layer 1 and between 1.4e-5 and 1.0e-3 at every layer 1..15 for z = 2+0.5i, 3+1i, 1+2i, i.e. O(1/n). Free-product moments tau(S^k), k=1,2,3, with a = W^T W (empirical or 2 MP_1: 2, 8, 40) and b = C_l agree with the empirical moments to 0.05-0.4% (m1), 0.2-1% (m2, 4% at layer 15), 0.5-4% (m3, 10% at layer 15); the depth-growing m3 discrepancy is the n^{-1/2} fluctuation of the collective spike (claim c2).
claims.consequence_for_system: Free probability describes the chain's covariance SPECTRUM per layer at O(1/n) accuracy; this is the origin of the cocycle effective-rank numbers of sec_cost.tex (reader's check: 1-2% at n=256, <1% at n=1024) and is useful only for design decisions (which ages to keep dense, rank thresholds), not for any quantity the estimator outputs.
claims.test: Already decisive: e1.log part 1. A cheaper re-check at any width is one eigh of C_l plus a 5000-step scalar iteration per z.

claims.claim: (a2) The NONLINEAR step C_l = F(S_l, m_l) is an entrywise Hermite map, not a spectral map; its large-n form is C_l = D_Phi S_l D_Phi + diag(v) + R with R the Hermite k>=2 off-diagonal part, ||R||_op/||C||_op = O(n^{-1/2}) (0.073 at layer 0 falling to 0.007 at layer 14 on net 0). So the Gaussian closure is a Dyson/free fixed point only at the level of spectral laws (law(S_{l+1}) = 2MP boxtimes law(D_Phi S_l D_Phi + diag v), the Fan–Wang/Pennington–Worah structure, with a realisation-dependent gate congruence D_Phi, Phi_a = Phi(alpha_a)), never at the level of per-neuron data. What the free picture drops, R, feeds the next layer's variances by d_a = (W R W^T)_aa / sigma_a^2 with EXACT zero ensemble mean (R is off-diagonal, E W_ab W_ac = 0 for b != c) but realisation rms 5.6e-4 to 1.2e-3, i.e. a mean shift of 3.3e-5 to 1.0e-4 per layer by the sensitivity law (F6).
claims.status: PROVED (decomposition and zero mean) + CHECKED (norms and feeds, e1.log part 2)
claims.argument: Cov(h_a,h_b) = sigma_a sigma_b sum_{k>=1} rho^k d_k(alpha_a) d_k(alpha_b)/k! (relu_gauss.py); the k=1 term is Phi_a Phi_b S_ab, the k>=2 off-diagonal terms are Hadamard powers of a matrix with O(n^{-1/2}) entries, hence O(n^{-1}) per entry and O(n^{-1/2}) in operator norm (sqrt(n) ||R||_op/||C||_op = 2.3 at layer 0, 0.2 at layer 14: the ratio shrinks faster than n^{-1/2} with depth because the collective spike grows). Measured feeds: d_a rms 5.6e-4 (layer 0) to 1.2e-3 (layer 7), mean -2.4e-5..+3.6e-5 (consistent with zero), shift rms 1.0e-4 -> 3.3e-5.
claims.consequence_for_system: Even for the Gaussian closure the 'free' (spectral, large-n) recursion is useless at the 1e-8 level: dropping R alone costs 3e-5 to 1e-4 per layer in the means, comparable with the exact chain's total error 1.9e-4 rms. The per-neuron Hadamard structure that free probability treats as vanishing noise is the same order as everything the system fights for.
claims.test: Done (e1.log). Decisive variant: run gauss_chain with R zeroed at every layer and compare with truth_off0; predicted MSE increase >= 1e-7 (cumulative 15 layers x 5e-5).

claims.claim: (a3) The third-cumulant chain is NOT the first non-planar / finite-width correction to the free (NNGP) closure: the identification is REFUTED. The kappa3 memory has zero mean over the weight ensemble at every order of 1/n (parity), typical size O(n^{-1/2}) (realisation fluctuation), and ensemble-mean square O(1/n); the even O(1/n) finite-width terms (the Roberts–Yaida–Hanin vertex) correspond in the realisation chain to the kappa4-type (radial scalar c4) and R-type terms, which are themselves realisation-specific at the 6-10% level.
claims.status: REFUTED (the identification); the replacement statements are PROVED (parity) and CHECKED (sizes)
claims.argument: At fixed upstream state and gates every kappa3 slice of z_l is a homogeneous cubic in W_l (K3_21 = slices_from_legs(W_l legs)), so E_{W_l} = 0 under W_l -> -W_l; the free Wick formula (paper Thm 2.30, non-crossing pair partitions) gives 0 for the same reason. CHECKED: |mean_M K3_3|/rms = 0.127 vs null 0.125 (n=256, M=64, e3_s1.log) and 0.359 vs null 0.354 (net 0, n=1024, M=8, e4.log); the reader's 0.0707 vs 0.0707 at M=200. Size: reader's rms_off(P)/rms_off(T S T^T) x sqrt(n) = 0.149, 0.149, 0.152, 0.142 at n = 64..512. Genus corrections of the weight ensemble (1/n for real Ginibre, 1/n^2 for unitarily invariant) are ensemble moments; the realisation's kappa3 is not a term of that expansion but the fluctuation about it. The radial scalar c4 (the chain's only kappa4) has relative spread 8.7-16% over W_l resamples at n=256 and 6.0% at n=1024 (e2 logs, e4.log) while the system needs it to ~1% (REPORT: c x 0.9 -> 2.5x MSE).
claims.consequence_for_system: No ensemble expansion (planar or non-planar, at any order) computes the memory; the chain's 12 n^3 per source-age is the price of the realisation's sign. The radial c4 is also not an ensemble quantity at the accuracy needed, so 'regenerate kappa4 from the ensemble' (the open-source chain's memoryless kappa4) must be a per-realisation computation, which the chain already does at O(n^2).
claims.test: c4 spread vs n: resample W_l at n = 256, 512, 1024 (e4_net0_wick.py pattern; 8 resamples suffice) and check rel std ~ n^{-1/2} (predicted 0.09, 0.064, 0.045; measured 0.087-0.097 and 0.060).

claims.claim: (b1) No free-model or classical conditional expectation that averages over W_l can reproduce the bulk hub pairing: E[P | anything independent of W_l] = 0 exactly, and E[P | W_l Pi_k] explains ~legE(k)^3 of its off-diagonal energy (reader: 0.15 at legE 0.51, 0.994 at legE 0.998), so holding the slice to 1e-3 needs 1 - legE ~ 3e-7, i.e. the full rank n/2 of the gated cocycle. Conditioning on the realisation's Gaussian-closure data (m_l, S_l) adds only the single direction mu: for C_{l-1} = I the conditional law of W_l given S_l is W_l = S_l^{1/2} O with O Haar, and E_O[P] = 0 while conditioning on m_l = S^{1/2} O mu confines the surviving part to terms with mean legs (the coherent/cross structure of Prop. parts).
claims.status: PROVED (parity, Haar argument for C = I; the legE^3 law is the reader's empirical fit) + CHECKED (reader's cond-mean vs Monte Carlo at noise level)
claims.argument: Oddness as in (a3). Haar: -I in O(n) kills odd polynomials; the stabiliser of mu in O(n) still contains the reflection -1 on mu^perp, so after conditioning on m_l the only surviving Wick/Haar terms carry at least one factor mu. The free potential of the paper contains only even powers of the free part (Lemma 2.32, Prop. 3.24), so an odd functional is nonzero only when all its variables are in the fixed part A(x), i.e. at t = 1 where the potential is the realised functional at full cost.
claims.consequence_for_system: F2/F3 restated as an information bound: the only part of the memory a derandomised surrogate can carry is the part that is a function of O(n) transported vectors (coherent/cross/diagonal), already measured (REPORT, oldmode=cross) to recover 1.65e-6 -> 1.2e-6 only.
claims.test: Reader's check_cond2.py is decisive; a one-direction version conditioning on mu (k=1, Pi = mu mu^T/|mu|^2) gives the Haar-stabiliser prediction: explained off-diagonal energy ~ legE(mu)^3 << 1.

claims.claim: (b2) The pairing's EFFECT on the final mean is NEITHER even nor odd in W_l, and its W_l-ensemble mean is NOT small: it carries 50% of the effect's energy, independent of n (0.47-0.52 at n=256, 0.500 at n=1024). The mechanism is exact and closed-form: the readout coefficients are odd in alpha_a = (W_l mu)_a/sigma_a (mean readout -alpha phi/(6 sigma^2); gates Phi(alpha) - 1/2; the Wick coefficients w(3,p) ~ He_1(alpha)), and the Wick pairing of one leg of the cubic with x_a = w_a . mu through the mean direction gives E[dmu_a] = E[x^3 F(x)] c3 + E[x F(x)] c1 with c3 = sum_q (A'mu)_q (B'mu)_q (C'mu)_q/|mu|^6 (three mean legs: coherent) and c1 = (2/n)/|mu|^2 sum_q [(C'mu)_q (A'^T P B')_qq + perms] (one mean leg + a hub-diagonal Wick pair: the CROSS/diagonal type), P = I - mu mu^T/|mu|^2. The cross term is 98-99% of the mean; the coherent term 1-2%.
claims.status: PROVED (Wick with sigma frozen) + CHECKED (e3_s1.log, e4.log): predicted mean -1.373e-3 vs measured -1.401e-3 +- 1.1e-5 (n=256, M=64; 2% from frozen sigma); -3.983e-4 vs -3.974e-4 +- 4.4e-6 (net 0, n=1024, layer 4, M=8; 0.2%); energy fraction pred 0.474/0.503 vs measured 0.493/0.500. Propagated to the final layer (n=256, L=8, readout at layer 4, two seeds): f^2 = 0.44-0.49 (seed 1), 0.41-0.52 (seed 2) at layers 4-7, null 1/M = 0.016-0.021; pairwise cosine between realisations 0.46/0.42 (null 0.06).
claims.argument: Row w_a ~ N(0, 2/n I) independent across a; split w = (x/|mu|^2) mu + w_perp; the cubic sum_q (w.A_q)(w.B_q)(w.C_q) averaged over w_perp leaves x^3 c3 + x c1; multiply by the odd coefficient F(x) and integrate (Gauss–Hermite). The n-independence follows because both the mean (c1 x) and the bulk rms scale as (2/n)^{3/2} times hub-space sums; their ratio is a cosine in hub space set by how collective the legs are (F7).
claims.consequence_for_system: REFUTES the reading of F2 as 'the memory's effect is mean-zero over the ensemble': the SLICE is mean-zero, its EFFECT is half ensemble-mean. But that half is exactly the O(n r) cross/diagonal Wick term (one mean leg plus (A^T B)_qq), the part already in the chain's exact readout and already measured (F2) to be worth less than a factor 2 in MSE; it does not help a cheaper system because the chain computes it anyway, and the other half (the realisation's bulk) is what costs n^3.
claims.test: Done (e3, e4). Decisive extension at full scale: kprop3c on net 0 with the old sources' readout replaced by the closed-form Wick mean c3 x^3 + c1 x per neuron (an O(n r) tier); predicted MSE ~ 1/2 of the 'dropped' value, i.e. ~1.7e-6 for window 2, matching the coherent+cross+diagonal line 1.2e-6 within the measured spread.

claims.claim: (b3) Under resampling of the TRANSPORT matrix W_{l+1} (the matrix that carries the kappa3 covariance feed dCh_l to the next layer's variances by the even quadratic form (W dCh W^T)_aa), the ensemble mean of the effect carries only 29-41% of its energy (f^2 = 0.29/0.37/0.41 seed 1, 0.31/0.36/0.40 seed 2 at layers 5-7), LESS than under resampling the matrix the pairing is cubic in. The free prediction of the covariance channel, (2/n) tr(dCh) (a radial rescaling of all variances), explains -18% (seed 1) and -1% (seed 2) of the first-order mean shift 1/2 w (W dCh W^T)_aa; the rank-1 (coherent) part of dCh explains 22%/11%; the ratio tr(dCh)/(sqrt2 ||dCh||_F) = 0.42/0.44 says dCh is incoherent (trace comparable with its Frobenius norm).
claims.status: CHECKED (e2_s1.log, e2_s2.log); evenness of the first-order channel PROVED
claims.argument: dmu_{l+1,a} = 1/2 w_a (W dCh W^T)_aa to first order (sensitivity law, d mu/d sigma^2 = phi/(2 sigma)); w_a = phi(alpha_a)/sigma_a is even in row a, the quadratic form is even, so the channel is even in W_{l+1} with mean (2/n) tr dCh and realisation fluctuation (2/n) sqrt2 ||dCh||_F per neuron: mean dominates only if tr dCh >> ||dCh||_F, which fails (ratio 0.42). Evenness guarantees a nonzero mean, not a dominant one. The other channels (mean feed W_{l+1} dmu_h,l — odd; continued kappa3 transport — cubic) have zero mean; the actual chain effect on mu_{l+1} (2.5e-3/2.9e-3 rms) is 2.5x the covariance channel and correlates 0.44/0.43 with it.
claims.consequence_for_system: A free surrogate for the transport of the memory's effect (replacing W_{l+1} by a semicircular family, which turns the covariance feed into a scalar trace, the 'radial' correction) captures nothing of the realisation's effect; the collective/radial direction is not where the kappa3 effect lives (consistent with F7: the exact chain's error is incoherent).
claims.test: Done. Cheapest full-scale confirmation: in kprop3c, replace the old sources' covariance feed by its trace (2/n) tr(dCh) I at each layer and compare with 'dropped': predicted no gain.

claims.claim: (b4) Surrogate ceiling: any derandomised or free surrogate of the kappa3 memory is a conditional expectation given a summary of the weights, hence the MSE-optimal estimator from that summary; the measured ensemble-mean fractions bound what it can capture at ~50% of the effect's energy (W_l summary) or ~35% (W_{l+1} summary), i.e. at most a factor 2 in the MSE contribution of the memory. The memory is worth a factor ~100 (window 2 dropped 3.7e-6 -> dense 3.5e-8), so a surrogate must capture >= 99% of the effect energy; it captures <= 50%.
claims.status: PROVED (optimality of the conditional mean under the Gaussian weight prior) + CHECKED (fractions, two seeds, two widths)
claims.argument: Energy not captured = (1 - f^2) x effect energy; with f^2 <= 0.5 the residual is >= half the dropped-memory error. Requirement: 1 - 1e-8/3.7e-6 = 99.7%.
claims.consequence_for_system: The free/derandomisation route to a cheaper memory is closed; the only remaining routes are those already named in our_problem.md (corrections of the EFFECT of dropped memory via Euler–Stein, or a change of what is computed), and for those the 50% ensemble-mean part is the cheap part the Euler–Stein defect need not explain, while the realisation bulk is what must reach rho >= 0.99 (sst reader M10).
claims.test: kprop3c oldmode=cross already is this test at full scale (1.65e-6 -> 1.2e-6); a sharper version replaces old slices by the Wick-mean tier of (b2).

claims.claim: (c1) The paper's replacement trick (hard conditional expectation -> computable potential tr x tau of the free model, Sec. 4.2, footnote 3, error per step ~ eta/n p^3 sigma^2 nu^2, Prop. 4.3) has as exact analogue the chain itself: the potential at t = 1 (all randomness fixed) is the realisation's chain, at t = 0 it is the NNGP/scalar recursion (eta(M) = (2/n) tr(M) I), and at intermediate t it is the conditional expectation given W_l Pi (the reader's cond_mean). The error calculus transfers with sigma nu = 2/sqrt(n): the per-neuron variance of the free (t=0) surrogate, (2/n) tr C_{l-1}, differs from the realisation's sigma_a^2 by 5.4% rms at layer 1 rising to 17.6% at layer 15 on net 0 (9.0% at layer 4 over W_4 resamples), i.e. mean shifts 5.8e-3 to 1.1e-2 per layer by F6: MSE ~1e-4, 25x worse than the Gaussian closure and 3000x worse than the chain. The collective eigenvalue lambda_1(S_l) fluctuates 4.6%/4.1%/2.7% at layers 6/12/15 under W_l resampling (2e-5 to 5e-5 per layer in the means by Prop. sens).
claims.argument: Both candidate potentials named in the task — the free resolvent of the gated cocycle and the operator-valued Stieltjes transform of the covariance — are tau of even functions of the weights and so are the t = 0 endpoint: they reproduce spectral laws (claim a1; reader's cocycle moments 1-2%) and nothing per neuron. Only the t = 1 endpoint reaches 1e-4 on variances, and it is the chain.
claims.consequence_for_system: There is no intermediate potential: partial derandomisation of a layer's weights loses (1 - legE) of the leg energy in the pair level and ~3(1 - legE) in the kappa3 level; the required 1e-6 leg-energy capture (sec_cost) means the whole realisation. The one usable transfer is the paper's error calculus, which is our sensitivity law: every replaced unit of randomness costs sigma nu = 2/sqrt(n) = 6% relative at n = 1024 against a 1e-4 requirement.
claims.test: Done (e1 part 3). A direct t-interpolation test: condition W_l on its top-k right singular directions of C_{l-1}^{1/2} and measure the per-neuron variance error vs k; predicted (1 - legE(k)) x 9% at layer 4.

claims.claim: (c2) What a free/derandomised surrogate CAN replace, with measured accuracy: spectral linear statistics tau(S_l), tau(S_l^2) (relative spread over W_l resamples 1.1%/4% at n=256, 0.34%/1.0% at n=1024: O(1/n) self-averaging), the MDE/Stieltjes transform (1e-4..1e-3), the cocycle's spectral moments and effective ranks (reader: 1-2%). What it CANNOT: the radial kappa4 scalar c4 (spread 8.7-16% at n=256, 6.0% at n=1024 vs ~1% needed), the collective eigenvalue (3-5%), per-neuron variances (5-18%), the R feed (zero mean, 3e-5-1e-4 per layer), every kappa3 slice (zero mean), the kappa3 effect (ceiling 50%).
claims.status: CHECKED (e1.log, e2 logs, e4.log) with the needed accuracies from REPORT.md/sec_central
claims.argument: Self-averaging holds for normalised traces of polynomials in the random matrix (CLT for linear statistics, O(1/n) relative) and fails for anything that is a per-neuron or per-entry quantity (O(n^{-1/2})), for spiked quantities (BBP outlier fluctuation O(n^{-1/2})), and for c4, which despite being an n^{-2}-normalised double sum is driven by the spike-correlated entries of K4h_22 and K3h_21 and fluctuates like a spiked statistic.
claims.consequence_for_system: Free-probability inputs belong in the design of the chain (ages kept dense, ranks of tiers: the crossover law L4 and the effective ranks 164, 92, 65, ...) and nowhere in its arithmetic. In particular the 'memoryless regeneration of kappa4' is not an ensemble computation.
claims.test: c4 and lambda_1 spread vs n (8 resamples per width, 3 widths) to pin the n^{-1/2} law; both quantities must then still be computed per realisation.

claims.claim: Caveats: the parity/effect measurements are on synthetic He nets (n=256, L=8, readout at layer 4; two seeds) and on one real layer (net 0, layer 4, direct readout only, M=8); the effect fractions at the final layer of the real network were not measured (each resample is a 41 s chain at n=1024). The Wick prediction freezes sigma_a at (2/n) tr C (2% bias at n=256, 0.2% at n=1024). 'Effect of the readout at layer l' zeroes K3_21, K3_3 at layer l only (covariance feed, mean readout and residual legs at l), the gated legs continue; alternative definitions (e.g. dropping a source's legs entirely) would change the fractions by the share of their later readouts, not the mechanism. The Haar argument of (b1) is exact for C_{l-1} = I and heuristic otherwise. No truth values exist for the synthetic nets, so all n=256 statements are about the structure of the effect, not about MSE.
claims.status: CONJECTURE (extrapolation of the 50% fraction to the final layer of the real network; the n^{-1/2} laws for c4 and lambda_1 beyond the two widths measured)
claims.consequence_for_system: None of the negative conclusions depends on the extrapolations: the ceiling (<= 50%) is an upper bound at both widths measured and the mechanism is closed-form.
claims.test: e2_effect_parity.py at n=1024 on net 0 with M=16 resamples of W_4 (about 2 x 16 x 12 layers x 20 s = 2 h on 2 threads) gives the real-network final-layer fraction.

verdict: Negative for the system, with one sharpening of F2. (a) The Gaussian closure is an operator-valued Dyson fixed point only in the weak sense: each linear step is exactly the scalar MDE g = 1/(z - (2/n) sum c_i/(z - 2 g c_i)) (residual 1e-4..1e-3 on net 0), and the entrywise ReLU step keeps the spectral law in the Fan–Wang form up to an O(n^{-1/2}) Hadamard remainder R; per-neuron variances fluctuate 5-18% about the free value, so the fixed point describes spectra, not the estimator. The third-cumulant chain is not the first finite-width correction: it is odd in each weight matrix (zero ensemble mean at every order, checked at n=256 and 1024), of typical size n^{-1/2}; the even O(1/n) terms (R, radial c4) are themselves realisation-specific at 6-10%. (b) No free/derandomised conditional expectation reproduces the bulk pairing (odd; Haar/Wick zero; legE^3 law). But the pairing's EFFECT on the mean is not mean-zero: because the readout coefficients are odd in alpha = W mu / sigma, its W_l-ensemble mean is a closed-form Wick contraction with the mean direction (predicted to 2%/0.2%), carrying 50% of the effect energy independent of n, and 98% of that mean is the cross term (one mean leg + hub-diagonal Wick pair), i.e. the cheap O(n r) part already known from F2 to be worth under a factor 2. Under resampling of the transport matrix the mean carries 29-41%, and the radial (free) surrogate of the covariance channel explains <= 0. A surrogate therefore captures <= 50% of the effect against the 99.7% required. (c) The paper's potential interpolates between the NNGP (t=0; variances off by 6-18%, MSE ~1e-4) and the realisation's chain (t=1); the candidate potentials (free resolvent of the cocycle, Stieltjes transform of the covariance) are the t=0 endpoint and replace only spectral linear statistics (0.3-1% at n=1024), never c4 (6%), lambda_1 (3-5%), per-neuron variances, or anything odd. Free probability belongs in the chain's design (ranks, windows), not in its arithmetic.
